metadata.goal: Understand how vessels organize themselves within a specific maritime corridor over the course of the day.
metadata.dataset_description: Constructed AIS-style observations in the open-water Fehmarn Belt. This sample contains 48 vessels and 1,136 observations within 00:00–16:00 on one constructed day. Raw downloaded Danish AIS files are unchanged.

insight_list.insight: Traffic is concentrated along a narrow through-corridor during the busier parts of the day, while lower-activity periods show more peripheral movement.

plot.title: Spatial concentration versus dispersion across four-hour activity windows
plot.description: Four maps share the same geographic extent and coastline. The busiest window (04:00–08:00, 24 vessels) shows a concentrated narrow corridor. The quieter windows contain mostly dispersed complete routes with differing directions, together with a minority of full corridor transits (00:00–04:00: 1 of 8 vessels; 08:00–12:00: 2 of 8 vessels; 12:00–16:00: 1 of 8 vessels). Each map labels its corridor and outside counts. Colors identify time windows, not route length. The lower charts show distinct active-vessel counts and each vessel's median absolute north-south offset from the GPS-derived corridor; dark lines mark window medians. Counts and offsets come from the same complete tracks. No claim is made about unsampled hours after 16:00.

insight_list.question: How does vessel activity organize itself spatially and temporally across the corridor?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the time chart with the mapped trajectories before describing the corridor pattern.
insight_list.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
def fit_corridor(frame):
    """Find the dominant GPS ridge without timestamps, speed or draught.

    Polynomial candidates come from geometrically well-conditioned tracks;
    the final score uses all positions. Neither track length nor longitude
    span is a peripheral/corridor classification rule.
    """
    x=frame['lon'].to_numpy();y=frame['lat'].to_numpy();candidates=[]
    for _,group in frame.groupby('trajectory_id'):
        if group.lon.max()-group.lon.min()>.12 and len(group)>=4:
            curve=np.polyfit(group.lon,group.lat,2)
            residual=np.abs(y-np.polyval(curve,x))*111.32
            candidates.append((np.count_nonzero(residual<.6),curve))
    curve=max(candidates,key=lambda row:row[0])[1]
    for _ in range(3):
        inlier=np.abs(y-np.polyval(curve,x))*111.32<.6
        curve=np.polyfit(x[inlier],y[inlier],2)
    # A fixed 0.8-km proximity band is stated on the map. The centerline is
    # estimated from observed coordinates, not an external lane attribute.
    return curve,.8/111.32

d=df.copy()
curve,half=fit_corridor(d)
# Lateral offset is the absolute north-south latitude residual, converted
# with 111.32 km/degree. It is not shortest geodesic distance to the curve.
d['lateral_offset_km']=np.abs(d.lat-np.polyval(curve,d.lon))*111.32
d['within_corridor']=d.lateral_offset_km.le(.8)
spatial=d.groupby('trajectory_id').agg(within_corridor_share=('within_corridor','mean'),median_lateral_offset_km=('lateral_offset_km','median'))
spatial['zone']=np.where(spatial.within_corridor_share.ge(.6),'Corridor vicinity','Outside corridor')
d['zone']=d.trajectory_id.map(spatial.zone)

d['timestamp']=pd.to_datetime(d['timestamp'])
d['period']=(d['timestamp'].dt.hour//4)*4
profile=d.groupby('period')['trajectory_id'].nunique().reindex([0,4,8,12],fill_value=0).rename('active_vessels').to_frame()
zone_counts=d.groupby(['period','zone']).trajectory_id.nunique().unstack(fill_value=0)
profile['corridor_vessels']=zone_counts['Corridor vicinity']
profile['outside_corridor_vessels']=zone_counts['Outside corridor']
vessel_offsets=d.groupby(['period','trajectory_id']).lateral_offset_km.median()
profile['median_vessel_lateral_offset_km']=vessel_offsets.groupby('period').median()
print(profile.round(3))
# Geographic comparison: use identical axes for all four windows.
fig,axes=plt.subplots(2,2,figsize=(14,7),sharex=True,sharey=True)
colors={0:'#946031',4:'#175dc4',8:'#995c96',12:'#087e7c'}
for ax,period in zip(axes.flat,[0,4,8,12]):
    for tid,g in d[d.period.eq(period)].groupby('trajectory_id'):
        g=g.sort_values('timestamp'); ax.plot(g.lon,g.lat,color=colors[period],alpha=.72)
    x=np.linspace(10.97,11.55,200)
    for delta in [-half,half]:ax.plot(x,np.polyval(curve,x)+delta,'--',color='#254b70',lw=.7)
    n=int(profile.loc[period,'active_vessels'])
    ax.set(xlim=(10.94,11.61),ylim=(54.49,54.665),title=f'{period:02d}:00–{period+4:02d}:00 | {n} vessels',xlabel='Longitude',ylabel='Latitude')
    ax.set_aspect(1/0.58)
plt.show()

evidence.spatial_group_rule: A vessel belongs to Corridor vicinity when at least 60% of its GPS positions have an absolute north-south offset of at most 0.8 km from the fitted ridge; otherwise Outside corridor. Track length is not a grouping rule; outside routes may cross the band.
evidence.corridor_definition: GPS-derived dominant quadratic ridge, scored against all observed positions and refined on its inliers. The dashed band is a fixed ±0.8 km north-south latitude offset. No external lane attribute, time, speed or draught enters its fit.
evidence.dispersion_metric: For each vessel, median(abs(latitude - fitted_latitude(longitude)) * 111.32) km; then the median across vessels in a window. This is north-south lateral offset, not shortest geodesic distance. Each vessel has equal weight.
evidence.observation_window: 00:00–16:00; counts measure activity within the selected sample, not population-level Danish AIS traffic.

computed_statistics.counting_unit: Distinct active vessel per window; trajectory_id is only a grouping key and maps one-to-one to vessel_id in this sample.

insight_list.insight: The corridor contains a mixture of steadily moving vessels and slower or nearly stationary tracks, creating different movement regimes within the same maritime area.

insight_list.question: What movement regimes coexist within the same corridor?

insight_list.insight: Vessels in the narrow through-corridor have noticeably deeper reported draughts than vessels using the corridor edges.

plot.title: Draught distributions by corridor position
plot.description: The map shows spatial groups defined by GPS proximity to the dominant ridge, independently of time and track length. Each dot in the right panel is one vessel draught; the horizontal line is the group median. The blue group has at least 60% of positions within the ±0.8 km band; the orange group contains all remaining tracks.

insight_list.question: How does reported vessel draught differ between the narrow through-corridor and its edges?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the full draught distributions and their overlap, not just the mean draught of each zone.
